title: Personal book collection - browse the catalogue and manage my books

sourcesRead.contributes: user story, context (/books, /profile, API contract pointer), accounts and test data, AC-1..AC-12 (table)
base URL and JSON bodies, Bearer auth, GenerateToken, account endpoints, error envelope and error table (1200/1205/1206/1210), Book object fields, BookStore endpoints with bodies, statuses and errors

context: A signed-in reader browses and searches the Book Store catalogue on /books and keeps a personal collection shown on /profile; clients manage the collection through the Book Store API specified in the attached api-contract.md (story.md#L17-L19, story.md#L23-L25). The API is on the same host as the web site and uses JSON bodies (attachments/api-contract.md#L3).

auth.mechanism: protected calls send Authorization: Bearer <token>; the token is obtained with POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken and body { "userName", "password" }
auth.credentials: the run's own user (unique user name, e.g. qa-<timestamp>) with the password from environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD (story.md#L29)

rules.text: All errors have the body { "code": "<string>", "message": "<string>" }; the error code is a string.

Book object fields: isbn (string), title (string), subTitle (string), author (string), publish_date (string, ISO-8601), publisher (string), pages (number), description (string), website (string, URL). Example: isbn "9781449325862", title "Git Pocket Guide", subTitle "A Working Introduction", author "Richard E. Silverman", publish_date "2020-06-04T08:48:39.000Z", publisher "O'Reilly Media", pages 234.

errorModel.case: Not authorized: no/invalid token, another user's userId on POST /BookStore/v1/Books, or another user's UUID on GET /Account/v1/User/{UUID}

errorModel.body: { "code": "1205", "message": "ISBN supplied is not available in Books Collection!" }
{ "code": "1206", "message": "ISBN supplied is not available in User's Collection!" }
{ "code": "1210", "message": "ISBN already present in the User's Collection!" }

testData.strategy: each run creates its own user through POST /Account/v1/User with a unique user name (for example qa-<timestamp>) and the password from environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD, and a token with POST /Account/v1/GenerateToken (story.md#L29-L30); books are added to that user's collection through POST /BookStore/v1/Books (AC-6, story.md#L42); AC-12's "another user's collection" cases (story.md#L48) need a second such user
constraints: books used in the examples are part of the standard catalogue, e.g. 9781449325862 "Git Pocket Guide", 9781593277574 "Understanding ECMAScript 6", 9781449331818 "Learning JavaScript Design Patterns" (story.md#L31)
the password comes from the environment variable DQ_USER_PASSWORD (story.md#L29)
testData.cleanup: delete each created user at the end with DELETE /Account/v1/User/{UUID}
